title: Coherent sheaves with free stalks are locally free
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent [pqf-def-coherent] $\mathcal O_X$-module. If every stalk $\mathcal F_x$ is a finite free $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module, then $\mathcal F$ is finite locally free on $X$.

proof.text: Use isCoherent_iff_isQuasicoherent_and_isFiniteType to install quasi-coherence and finite type. Apply isFiniteLocallyFree_of_isAffineOpen, reducing to finite presentation and flatness of sections on each affine open. The finite-type affine sections theorem gives finite generation, hence finite presentation over the Noetherian section ring.

For an affine open U and each maximal ideal of its section ring, identify the corresponding point y of U. The existing affine germ localization theorem supplies the localization map from sections to the stalk. The finite-free stalk hypothesis and the base-change characterization of localized modules make the localized section module free, hence flat. Localized maximal flatness then yields flatness of the section module, completing the affine criterion.
The affine criterion applied on every affine open is exactly finite local freeness.

proof_origin.note: Uses existing affine local freeness criterion and affine germ localization directly.
